verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘You shall be holy; for I, Yahweh your God, am holy.
“‘Each one of you shall respect his mother and his father. You shall keep my Sabbaths. I am Yahweh your God.
“‘Don’t turn to idols, nor make molten gods for yourselves. I am Yahweh your God.
“‘When you offer a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh, you shall offer it so that you may be accepted.
It shall be eaten the same day you offer it, and on the next day: and if anything remains until the third day, it shall be burned with fire.
If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination. It will not be accepted;
but everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the holy thing of Yahweh, and that soul shall be cut off from his people.
“‘When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners of your field, neither shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
You shall not glean your vineyard, neither shall you gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am Yahweh your God.
“‘You shall not steal. “‘You shall not lie. “‘You shall not deceive one another.
“‘You shall not swear by my name falsely, and profane the name of your God. I am Yahweh.
“‘You shall not oppress your neighbor, nor rob him. “‘The wages of a hired servant shall not remain with you all night until the morning.
“‘You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind; but you shall fear your God. I am Yahweh.
“‘You shall do no injustice in judgment. You shall not be partial to the poor, nor show favoritism to the great; but you shall judge your neighbor in righteousness.
“‘You shall not go up and down as a slanderer among your people. “‘You shall not endanger the life  of your neighbor. I am Yahweh.
“‘You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
“‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
“‘You shall keep my statutes. “‘You shall not cross-breed different kinds of animals. “‘You shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed; “‘Don’t wear a garment made of two kinds of material.

“‘If a man lies carnally with a woman who is a slave girl, pledged to be married to another man, and not ransomed, or given her freedom; they shall be punished. They shall not be put to death, because she was not free.
He shall bring his trespass offering to Yahweh, to the door of the Tent of Meeting, even a ram for a trespass offering.
The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering before Yahweh for his sin which he has committed: and the sin which he has committed shall be forgiven him.
“‘When you come into the land, and have planted all kinds of trees for food, then you shall count their fruit as forbidden.  Three years they shall be forbidden to you. It shall not be eaten.
But in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, for giving praise to Yahweh.
In the fifth year you shall eat its fruit, that it may yield its increase to you. I am Yahweh your God.
“‘You shall not eat any meat with the blood still in it. You shall not use enchantments, nor practice sorcery.
“‘You shall not cut the hair on the sides of your head or clip off the edge of your beard.
“‘You shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor tattoo any marks on you. I am Yahweh.
“‘Don’t profane your daughter, to make her a prostitute; lest the land fall to prostitution, and the land become full of wickedness.
“‘You shall keep my Sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary; I am Yahweh.
“‘Don’t turn to those who are mediums, nor to the wizards. Don’t seek them out, to be defiled by them. I am Yahweh your God.
“‘You shall rise up before the gray head, and honor the face of an old man, and you shall fear your God. I am Yahweh.
“‘If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you in your land, you shall not do him wrong.

The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.
“‘You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, of weight, or of quantity.
You shall have just balances, just weights, a just ephah,  and a just hin. I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
“‘You shall observe all my statutes, and all my ordinances, and do them. I am Yahweh.’”

footnotes.content: Moses listens at the threshold of mystery—the Lord speaks, and his words reshape a whole people. This is how holiness begins: not with our effort, but with His voice reaching into our ordinary days.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "You shall be holy; for I, Yahweh your God, am holy." The Lord names the reason before the command. We are called to reflect His character, not because the law demands it, but because He is already holy and loves us enough to draw us toward what He is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Respect for mother and father sits at the heart of holiness—the first human bond He names. And the Sabbath rest: both honor creation's order and trust His rhythm. A holy life begins at home, in the small room where we learn to obey and to rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Idols are handmade gods—things our hands can control, unlike the living Lord who calls us into mystery. To turn from idols is to say: I will not build a god small enough for me to understand. I will bow to the One who is wholly Other.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peace offerings brought joy to Israel's feasts—a gift of gratitude, shared at table. The gift only works if the heart is right. Sacrifice without surrender is noise to the Lord. He reads what lies beneath every gesture.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sacrifice binds time—eaten today and tomorrow, but not the third day. It teaches an old lesson: the holy cannot be hoarded. What is offered to God must be consumed in its season, not stored up in fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An abomination—the word strikes hard. To eat spoiled meat is to treat the holy carelessly, as though the Lord's gift were common. It whispers that respect for the sacred is not a small thing; it shapes the soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "That soul shall be cut off from his people." The consequence falls on those who profane the holy thing—not by accident, but by willful disregard. It shows that covenant-breaking has a weight that the community cannot ignore.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Leave the corners of your field unharvested—an ancient mercy written into the harvest itself. Ruth will one day glean there, poor and foreign, and find not scraps but dignity. The law that feeds the stranger is the law of love planted in rows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "You shall leave them for the poor and for the foreigner." The vineyard teaches the same grace: don't strip it bare. The poor and the stranger have a claim on the harvest you didn't plant—because you once lived as a stranger in Egypt, and the Lord remembered you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three commands stand together: don't steal, don't lie, don't deceive. They anchor holiness in the small, daily truth—the way we handle what belongs to another, the word we speak when no one is watching, the mask we drop when the stranger isn't looking.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To swear falsely by God's name is to use His holiness as a tool for deception—to pull Him into your lie. The Lord warns: when you invoke My name, My character is at stake. Your word becomes a witness to what I am.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pay the hired worker his wage by morning—don't make him wait, let him fret through the night. The law remembers what he feels: anxiety about bread for his family. To withhold wages is to steal not just money but rest and dignity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't mock the deaf or trip the blind—they cannot see your cruelty coming. The law protects those who are most vulnerable. And it reaches deep: to mock the vulnerable is to forget that the Lord sees everything we think we hide from sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Judge righteously: not favoring the poor out of pity, not favoring the great out of fear. Justice demands that we see each person truly, stripped of circumstance. It's harder than kindness; it asks for clarity when emotion pulls us crooked.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't slander your neighbor, don't endanger his life. The first kills his name in secret; the second takes it openly. Both break the thin trust that holds a people together. The Lord sees what we whisper as plainly as what we shout.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't hate your brother in your heart—pull out the root before the fruit spoils. If he wrongs you, rebuke him face to face rather than letting bitterness fester alone. True love tells the hard truth; it doesn't let him destroy himself in silence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Love your neighbor as yourself." This verse will echo through all Scripture—Jesus will name it as second only to the love of God. It's the hinge on which all mercy turns: you already know what you need; give that same measure to another.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't cross-breed animals, don't sow two kinds of seed, don't wear cloth of mixed thread. These laws teach order—keep the kinds distinct, preserve the boundaries that the Lord has set in creation. Order in small things prepares the heart to honor His order in all things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A man lies with a slave woman pledged to another—it's sin, but she's not to blame, for she was not free to choose. The law marks a hard boundary: she is not his to take. Even her powerlessness cannot make the wrong right.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A trespass offering—the guilty man must bring a ram to the Tent of Meeting. He cannot hide what he has done; he must face the priest, face the Lord, and pay the cost. Restoration always begins with naming the wrong.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest makes atonement; the sin is forgiven. Grace is not free—it costs the ram, it costs the priest's intercession. But it is offered. He will not be cast away forever. Even this sin, brought into the light, can be restored.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Plant a tree—it will not feed your children for three years. This law teaches long obedience, the willingness to sow for a harvest you may not eat. It shapes a people who think beyond today, who trust that the Lord has tomorrow in His hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the fourth year, the fruit is holy—given to praise the Lord. The harvest belongs to Him first. To hold the first fruits means the whole harvest becomes an act of worship, a way of saying: This is Yours, and I am glad.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the fifth year, finally, you eat and the tree yields its increase. The law teaches patience rewarded—the waiting shapes the eater. By the time the fruit is yours, you have learned that all fruitfulness flows from His hand, and your satisfaction will be deeper.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't eat meat with blood still in it; don't use enchantments or practice sorcery. The Lord forbids practices that claim power apart from Him—magic that treats the unseen as a tool to wield, rather than a mystery to revere.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't cut the hair on the sides of your head, don't clip the edge of your beard. These marks set Israel apart—a visible boundary that says: we belong to the Lord. The body itself becomes a witness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't make cuttings in your flesh for the dead or tattoo marks on you. The body is not for you to inscribe with sorrow or magic. It belongs to the Lord—the Lord of life, not the dead. Grieve, but let grief draw you toward Him, not into ritual that binds you to the past.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't profane your daughter by making her a prostitute—the land itself will fall into wickedness if you traffic in your own flesh. The law protects the vulnerable and warns that injustice spreads. What corrupts one soul ripples outward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Keep the Sabbaths and reverence the sanctuary—two forms of the same obedience. The Sabbath teaches rest; the sanctuary teaches approach. Together they anchor Israel between work and worship, between the world and the holy place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't seek mediums or wizards—don't reach toward the dead to know the future or the hidden. The Lord alone is your God. To seek elsewhere is to distrust His guidance and to let fear pull you into practices that defile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rise before the gray head and honor the old man. You are honoring not just a person but the Lord who carried them this far. An older life is a long lesson in God's faithfulness. Listen to them; their years are a gift.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The stranger among you—do him no wrong. Israel was once strangers in Egypt, powerless and far from home. Memory shapes mercy. To welcome the foreigner is to remember that the Lord remembered you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt." The law gives the reason—history is a teacher of grace. Your own exile becomes the mandate to welcome. The Lord's memory of your need becomes the measure of your mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, of weight, or of quantity. Even in the marketplace, in the scales and measures, holiness must be present. A false weight is a lie. A short measure is theft. The Lord is watching.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Just balances, just weights, a just ephah and hin—the tools themselves must be true. "I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt." The One who freed you from slavery watches how you treat those who buy and sell. Justice matters everywhere.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "You shall observe all my statutes, and all my ordinances, and do them." Readers today hear an echo of a life oriented toward obedience—not to earn love, but because the One who loves you has shown you the way. The commands are guardrails on a path toward freedom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
